message.content:
Below are three practical ways to grab a snapshot of a web page with Python.  
Pick the one that best matches your workflow:

| Goal | Recommended tool | Why |
|------|------------------|-----|
| **Open a URL, render it, and grab a screenshot** | **Selenium + ChromeDriver** | Works everywhere, supports head‑less mode, easy to install. |
| **Open a URL, render it, and grab a screenshot (modern)** | **Playwright** | Faster, supports multi‑browser, has a “full‑page” flag out of the box. |
| **Capture the *currently* displayed page in an already‑running Chrome** | **Chrome DevTools Protocol (`pychrome`)** | Connects to an existing Chrome instance (must have been launched with `--remote-debugging-port`). |

---

## 1️⃣ Selenium – the classic, battle‑tested approach

```bash
pip install selenium webdriver-manager
```

```python
from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.service import Service
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options
from webdriver_manager.chrome import ChromeDriverManager

# ---------- Setup ----------
opts = Options()
opts.add_argument("--headless")          # no GUI
opts.add_argument("--disable-gpu")
opts.add_argument("--window-size=1920,1080")  # optional: set viewport size

service = Service(ChromeDriverManager().install())   # auto‑download matching chromedriver
driver = webdriver.Chrome(service=service, options=opts)

# ---------- Navigate & Screenshot ----------
url = "https://www.example.com"
driver.get(url)

# Full‑page screenshot (requires Selenium 4.8+)
driver.save_screenshot("screenshot.png")

# ---------- Clean up ----------
driver.quit()
```

> **Tip:**  
> *If you need a screenshot of a particular element:*  
> ```python
> elem = driver.find_element(By.CSS_SELECTOR, "#main")
> elem.screenshot("elem.png")
> ```

---

## 2️⃣ Playwright – modern, fast, and feature‑rich

```bash
pip install playwright
playwright install  # downloads Chromium, Firefox, WebKit binaries
```

```python
import asyncio
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

async def run():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        # Launch Chromium (or p.firefox / p.webkit)
        browser = await p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
        page = await browser.new_page(viewport={"width": 1920, "height": 1080})
        
        await page.goto("https://www.example.com")
        
        # Full‑page screenshot (no extra code needed)
        await page.screenshot(path="screenshot.png", full_page=True)
        
        await browser.close()

asyncio.run(run())
```

> **Why Playwright?**  
> *Built‑in `full_page=True` flag.*  
> *Supports mobile emulation, screenshots of individual elements, PDFs, etc.*

---

## 3️⃣ Capture the *current* Chrome window (already running)

### Prerequisites

```bash
pip install pychrome pillow
```

> **Important:**  
> The Chrome instance you want to capture **must have been started with**  
> `--remote-debugging-port=9222` (or another free port).  
> Example command line:  
> ```
> google-chrome --remote-debugging-port=9222
> ```

### Code

```python
import base64
import json
import os
import pychrome
from PIL import Image
from io import BytesIO

# ---------- Connect to the running Chrome ----------
browser = pychrome.Browser(url="http://127.0.0.1:9222")  # default port
tabs = browser.list_tab()
if not tabs:
    raise RuntimeError("No Chrome tabs found. Is Chrome running with --remote-debugging-port?")
tab = tabs[0]  # pick the first tab; you can filter by URL if you like

# ---------- Grab a screenshot ----------
tab.start()
tab.call_method("Page.enable")
tab.call_method("Page.navigate", url="https://www.example.com")
tab.wait(2)  # give the page some time to load

# Grab the screenshot (base64 encoded PNG)
result = tab.call_method("Page.captureScreenshot", format="png")
data = result["data"]

# Decode and save
image_bytes = base64.b64decode(data)
with open("screenshot.png", "wb") as f:
    f.write(image_bytes)

tab.stop()
```

> **What you get:**  
> *A PNG of the rendered page (viewport only).*  
> *If you want a full‑page screenshot, add `clip` arguments or use `Page.captureScreenshot` with `captureBeyondViewport:true` (requires Chrome 86+).*

---

## Bonus: Grab the *visible* part of an already‑open Chrome window (no DevTools)

If you cannot restart Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port`, you can still grab the pixels that are actually on your screen:

```bash
pip install mss pygetwindow
```

```python
import mss
import pygetwindow as gw
import mss.tools

def capture_chrome_window(output_path="screenshot.png"):
    # Find the first Chrome window
    windows = gw.getWindowsWithTitle("Google Chrome")
    if not windows:
        raise RuntimeError("Could not find a Chrome window.")
    win = windows[0]

    # Coordinates of the client area (exclude title bar, borders)
    left, top = win.left, win.top
    width, height = win.width, win.height

    # Optional: adjust for OS-specific chrome UI height
    # e.g., on Windows, subtract ~30px for the title bar
    # height -= 30

    bbox = {"top": top, "left": left, "width": width, "height": height}

    with mss.mss() as sct:
        img = sct.grab(bbox)
        mss.tools.to_png(img.rgb, img.size, output=output_path)

capture_chrome_window()
```

> **Pros:** No need to restart Chrome.  
> **Cons:** Captures the *entire* window, including tabs, address bar, etc.  
> *If you need only the web content area, you’ll have to subtract the UI height manually.*

---

## Quick checklist

| Step | What to do | Command / snippet |
|------|------------|-------------------|
| 1 | Install dependencies | `pip install selenium webdriver-manager` or `pip install playwright && playwright install` |
| 2 | Choose a method | Selenium (classic), Playwright (modern), or DevTools (existing Chrome) |
| 3 | Run the script | `python screenshot.py` |
| 4 | Verify output | Look for `screenshot.png` in your working directory |

Happy coding! 🚀
